newsitem.title: UK: Talk of firmer Panamaxes stirs Ldn freight.
newsitem.headline: Talk of firmer Panamaxes stirs Ldn freight.

text.p: A generally dull dry cargo market was enlivened on the last day of the year by reports of Pananax activity in the US Gulf/Far East trades where brokers said that firmer rates are understood to have been conceded by charterers.

Strengthening conditions in the Gulf are attracting modern Panamaxes in ballast in the North Pacific. In addition owners' brokers are optimistic about New Year prospects of increased demand from grain and coal charterers from Australia and S Africa, especially for Panamaxes.

Severe weather in the northern hemisphere is cited by owners as likely to stimulate coal trading. Very little Caper news has become available and the Handysize market remains dull in most areas. The BFI was unchanged at 1516.

There has been a flurry of activity in the US Gulf/Japan grain trades. Reports circulated overnight that Klaveness had relet Legiony Polskie at a weaker $26.50 combo and that MSK had fixed Madonna Lily for 52,000 soyabeans for Jan 10/20 at $26.25 combo.

These were succeeded today by rumours that Andre had fixed a similar position at a much firmer $27.25 combo. Andre were also linked with the Yukong-relet Drin 73,087 dwt, in ballast from Honolulu Dec 23, delivery US Gulf mid-Jan trip Japan at $15,700 daily plus $310,000 bonus. On a rough calculation, if $27.00 combo US Gulf/Japan equates to around $11,000 daily for a vessel making round voyage from East Asia, more tonnage from the Pacific can be expected to follow suit.

But owners' brokers report substantial potential demand for Panamaxes for grain from Australia to Egypt, Iran, Pakistan and Sri Lanka in the New Year. Initially this should benefit especially vessels in S E Asia and the Indian Ocean, but may also in due course attract tonnage open in Japan and S Korea.

Panamaxes have been fixed on private terms in grain from NoPac to Bin Qasim.Metalink is one charterer involved, possibly having taken early 1980's-built Panamax tonnage basis delivery Far East at $10,000/10,250 daily. Elsewhere grain market rumours linked ADM with about 40,000 heavy grain USNH/Continent, and Dreyfus with Mentese 53,000 dwt for about 40,000 grains 55' US Gulf to France at about $15.50/16.00.

In the absence of apparent Caper involvement, Panamaxes were widely reported booked for Atlantic loading. Capitano Giovanni 74,500 dwt, another vessel in ballast from the Far East, was fixed by Koch Carbon delivery US Gulf mid Jan trip Japan with petcoke at a strong $16,250 daily plus $330,000 bonus.

The Torm-relet Captain George l 64,000 dwt was understood fixed US Gulf/China on private terms, and Samsun booked Tatry 66,088 dwt delivery el Ferrol early Jan trip via Kpeme with bauxite to the Philippines at $15,500 daily.

There was confusion about Seyang's fixture of Dimitris Perrotis 64,000 dwt but brokers reckoned the fixture was for fertlizers to China basis delivery Morehead City at $14,250 daily plus $305,000 bonus or US Gulf at $14,500 plus $335,000/340,000. In the East, Golden Glow 63,990 dwt was rumoured booked by Aimcor or SSM for petcoke California/ Continent and Noble were linked with the 20-year old Panamax Pearl 61,803 dwt delivery prompt PMO or Goa trip China at $9,600 daily.

Grant were said to have taken a Handymax on private terms Brazil/Far East, and Moller a Turkish-controll 43,000 dwt vessel Black Sea/Far East at about $11,250 daily. In the North Pacific Navix fixed an over-age 35,000 dwt craned vessel delivery Vancouver trip S E Asia with grain at $7,400 daily plus $140,000 bonus.
